sources.source: Apache Iceberg table specification, Deletion Vectors

items.item: deletion vectors identify deleted rows of a file by encoding deleted positions in a bitmap; a set bit at position P means the row at P is deleted

at.step: Reveal: a deletion vector is a bitmap, not a list

items.item: there can be at most one deletion vector per data file in a snapshot, more efficient at execution time than position delete files

at.step: Reveal: the same bitmap, three formats, one real difference

sources.source: Apache Hudi, Table and Query Types

items.item: merge-on-read deletes are written as records directly into log files, merged dynamically with base files during query execution — no bitmap

at.step: Reveal: the same bitmap, three formats, one real difference

items.item: a cardinality at or under 4,096 indicates an array container; above it indicates a bitset container

at.step: Predict: what happens once the deletion count crosses that threshold?
Reveal: reproduced for real — a large deletion vector becomes a bitset

items.item: The data file in examples.py is plain CSV text, not Parquet, and the container implementation is a simplified reimplementation of the Roaring format (reusing its real 4,096-element array/bitset threshold and 65,536-bit single-container bitset size) rather than the real RoaringBitmap library's run-length containers or on-disk serialization byte for byte — disclosed in the script's own docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1 and #2.

The claim that Delta and Iceberg share the bitmap format specifically (not just the same idea by different names, this chapter's earlier topic-14 framing) is sourced directly from the Puffin spec's own big-endian-for-Delta-compatibility text, a stronger and more specific claim that needed its own citation — FACT-CHECK.md red-team #3.

at.step: Reveal: the same bitmap, three formats, one real difference

items.item: Hudi is deliberately not described as having 'an equivalent deletion vector' — its docs never use that term for its MOR log-file deletes, and this topic frames it as a different architectural answer to the same question, not a bitmap by another name — FACT-CHECK.md red-team #4.

at.step: Reveal: the same bitmap, three formats, one real difference

items.item: The read-cost demo's 'compaction' is a plain purge-and-rewrite of the CSV file, not a real columnar rewrite or a real query engine's physical plan change — the cost shape (DV-applied scan costs more, post-compaction scan costs less) is what transfers, consistent with topics 13 and 14's established disclosure pattern.

No flaky-timing issue was hit in this topic's examples.py, unlike topic 14's isolated-merge-prep fix — the deletion-vector lookup's added per-row cost is large enough relative to this sandbox's I/O noise to assert directly with a 9-repeat median, verified robust across 5 consecutive runs.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — compaction pays that cost back

items.item: The on-screen counts (1,200; 5,000; 50,000; 2,400 bytes; 8,192 bytes) are all literal constants or literal-asserted values in examples.py, not values computed at runtime from a fraction, so the build's digit-provenance check can trace every one of them to executed truth.

items.item: Iceberg's spec text that a DV, once written, must replace all previously written position delete files for that data file is covered by this topic's sources but not individually dramatized on screen, since the reel's 10-step budget focuses on the array/bitset tradeoff and the cross-format comparison rather than Iceberg's own file-replacement bookkeeping rules.
